lines.text: How can a tiny songbird fly five thousand miles across oceans and land in the exact same backyard tree every year?
Birds possess navigational abilities that surpass modern human military guidance systems.
They use the position of the sun during the day, and memorized star constellations at night.
They even smell atmospheric odor gradients to track geographic river coastlines.
Most mind-blowing of all, birds possess quantum compasses in their eyes.
Special proteins called cryptochromes allow birds to literally see Earth's invisible magnetic field lines as shades of light.
Birds navigate the globe using quantum physics built directly into their retinas.
